gg_coo_a.text: The coolet gives you a long, fringed look, chews, and returns to the matter of the grass.

gg_coo_b.text: The coolet's fringe is so long it's a miracle it can see. It seems to manage fine.

gg_kelpie.text: The kelpie stands in the shallows, perfectly still. It is looking at you, and you are quite sure the water is looking too.

gg_lockkeeper.text: Eight locks, one after the other. We call it Neptune's Staircase. A boat takes about ninety minutes to climb it, and about nine minutes to feel smug about it.
The Caledonian Canal opened in 1822. Thomas Telford planned it so that ships needn't round the north of Scotland. Many still don't know it's here.

gg_cyclist.text: Seventy-nine miles, Fort William to Inverness. I'm on day three. My feet have introduced themselves.
It's mostly canal towpath and forest track. It's flat, they said. Then they showed me the hills.

gg_monsterwatcher.text: I've been watching this loch for ten years. I've seen sixty-two swans, nine seals, and one very suspicious log.
The big one's up at Loch Ness, further along. I come down here for the practice.

gg_boatman.text: The canal's a short cut for yachts, fishing boats, and the odd kayaker who's lost faith in the sea.
At the top of the staircase the water's about twenty metres higher than at the bottom, which is just how Telford wanted it. The boats find it quite a view.

gate_great_glen.text: Loch Ness is closed. Director's survey. Only she can wave you through.
She's back in Glencoe, in the mist, in orange wellies. She's been expecting you. She said so twice, and then wrote it down.
